title: Length-tier prefetch coordinator to stabilize continuous batching for mixed-length dialogs
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (chat apps with long system prompts + very short user turns, support dialogs with long context and short responses) cause three operational issues for the continuous batcher: 1) KV cache fragmentation and high residency for a small fraction of sessions, 2) inefficient slot packing where long-turns block batch progress and increase tail latency, and 3) GPU memory spike events during lane demotion or cold prefetch that trigger OOMs or aggressive eviction policies.

Goal: Implement a length-tier prefetch coordinator that layers admission control, predictive prefetching and memory-aware slot assignment to reduce tail latency and KV pressure while preserving throughput. Targets: reduce 95th-percentile generation latency by ~20% on mixed workloads, reduce KV cache churn by 15-25%, and eliminate OOM spikes from mixed-length bursts in canary clusters.

Design overview:
- Admission tiers: classify incoming requests into three length tiers (short, medium, long) using a light-weight estimator (token-length + historical turn size). Tiers determine prefetch policy and reserved slot allocation.
- Predictive prefetch worker: for medium/long tiers, prefetch likely prefix KV segments proactively using a small LRU-backed warmup buffer per GPU to avoid cold-KV stalls during generation. Prediction uses a configurable n-gram length estimate + recent session history.
- Reservoir slots: reserve a small fraction of continuous-batcher slots for long turns to avoid head-of-line blocking. These slots maintain longer KV residency but are limited in number and tracked with strict watermarks.
- Memory-aware eviction: implement tier-aware KV eviction thresholds: short-tier eviction is more aggressive, long-tier is conservative. When overall GPU memory utilization crosses a soft watermark, prefetch is throttled and long-tier reservoir admission is reduced.
- Length-coalescing micro-batches: within the batcher, prefer coalescing requests of similar length tiers to reduce per-token compute variance and improve kernel utilization.
- Metrics & signals: new metrics: kv_residency_by_tier, prefetch_hit_ratio, tier_slot_utilization, tier_tail_latency_p95, gpu_soft_watermark_events. Integrate with Console dashboards and alerts.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Prototype: implement coordinator as an opt-in scheduler hook in continuous-batcher (C++) + a small predictive prefetch Rust worker storing per-GPU warm buffers. (2 sprints)
2) Integration tests: unit tests for admission and eviction logic; synthetic harness for mixed-length traffic; local GPU smoke tests. (1 sprint)
3) Canary: staged rollout to a small dedicated pool (canary1) with telemetry enabled and automatic rollback thresholds based on tail latency and OOM events. (1 sprint)
4) Rollout: expand to more clusters with gradual increases in reservoir fraction and prefetch aggressiveness; track regression alerts and cost signals. (2-3 sprints)

Acceptance criteria:
- prefetch_hit_ratio > 60% for medium/long tiers on synthetic benchmark;
- kv_residency_by_tier shows >15% reduction in churn for short-tier;
- p95 latency improves >=15% on mixed workload;
- no increase in OOM incidents during canary (zero regressions).

Testing and benchmarks:
- Use existing mixed-length harness in perf-lab (scripts linked below). Add scenarios: high-concurrency chat, episodic long-context generation, and bursty short-turns.
- Run A/B test against control continuous-batcher for token cost, latency distributions, and GPU memory patterns.

Rollout & safety:
- Canary stop conditions: p95 latency regression >5% for 10 minutes OR any OOM event OR prefetch_hit_ratio < 30% for 5 minutes.
- Gradual throttle knobs: prefetch_rate, reservoir_fraction, eviction_bias. Default off for hosted customers; enable behind feature-flag for Dedicated-only initially.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: misprediction increases KV churn. Mitigation: conservative default prefetch (n=1 lookahead) and quick disable via feature flags.
- Risk: new coordination code could add scheduling latency. Mitigation: keep coordinator decision path O(1) and async prefetch worker on separate thread pool.
- Risk: complexity increases operational burden. Mitigation: expose concise metrics and a runbook for operators with clear rollback steps.

Open questions:
- What is the correct default reservoir_fraction for 8xA100 pools? (proposal: 6-8%)
- Should prefetch be model-aware (longer context models get more aggressive prefetch)? (defer to model-owner API work)
